name: English
title: Open Agent Systems — Open foundations for AI-native systems
description: Open foundations connecting models, agents, tools, data and compute for AI systems that can run, be governed and evolve.
label: An open-source organization
headline:
Connect intelligence.
Evolve systems.
intro: From a model call to systems that keep doing real work. Open Agent Systems builds toward open foundations for the AI-native era.
introMore: Connect models, agents, tools, data and compute so independent capabilities can work together and innovation can reach real use.
aboutText: As AI moves from answering questions to taking action, teams need reusable foundations, controlled costs and verifiable delivery. These are the outcomes we aim to support.
areas: Reduce repeated integration and environment setup so teams can focus on their work.
Connect model usage, task budgets and environment lifecycles to make costs visible.
Build permissions, execution evidence and result verification into workflows.
Share skills, knowledge, templates and practices while preserving choice and portability.
directionTitle: From open components to a connected ecosystem
directionIntro: We expect the work to move from individual tools toward connected systems. Each step should build on working software and lessons from its users.
steps: Build model access, execution, asset management and verification around real needs. Each component should stand on its own.
Connect projects through clear interfaces and compatibility checks, linking tasks, identity, assets and evidence.
Explore collaboration across local, private-cloud, public-cloud and edge environments with explicit data and portability boundaries.
Explore trusted delegation and capability distribution across organizations, with improvements evaluated and reviewed before release.
feedbackLoop: Real use and community feedback inform every stage.
directionNote: This diagram describes our intended direction, not a release schedule or a statement of completed capabilities. Work in these areas may overlap; priorities will follow actual needs and available contributions.
principles: Prefer small, composable capabilities with understandable interfaces.
Documentation, examples, and maintainability matter alongside implementation.
Be clear about what is available, what has been verified, and what is still being explored.
joinText: Have a use case, an integration problem, or an idea for the ecosystem? Tell us what you’re trying to do, what is getting in the way, and what you’ve already tried.
joinNote: Organization-level suggestions are welcome in the community repository’s Issues. Contributions to individual projects will be handled in their own repositories when they are published.
footer: Open foundations for the AI-native era.
architectureIntro: Explore how eight capability domains work together. Choose a task path to highlight its capabilities, or select any domain to inspect its role.
architectureNote: Ecosystem plan and conceptual interaction. Intended capabilities and relationships, not shipped products or live telemetry.
layers: Govern model access, traffic, credentials and costs while preserving choice of providers.
Coordinate planning, delegation and long-running work around explicit goals and acceptance criteria.
Provide controlled code, browser and desktop environments from provisioning to suspension, recovery and cleanup.
Separate what a model sees from durable task facts, with traceable knowledge and bounded access.
Make prompts, skills, tools, agents and environment templates verifiable, reusable and traceable.
Carry identity, permissions and budgets through calls and execution with explicit accountability.
Turn task evidence into diagnosis, evaluated changes and controlled releases.
Bring shared capabilities into everyday development and validate them through real workflows.
visionTitle: From individual capabilities to shared foundations.
visionText: Developers should be able to choose models, compose capabilities and control execution. Teams should turn their work into reusable assets, while independent projects evolve together through open interfaces.
exploreNote: Concept exploration · Select a node to see its role
exploreItems: Connect different models so applications can choose and switch capabilities for the task.
Combine models, skills, and tools into execution units that can carry out tasks.
Bring external tools and data into intelligent systems through understandable interfaces.
Provide observable, manageable environments for intelligent execution.
Compose underlying capabilities into products developers and teams can actually use.
directionHint: Select a direction to explore the work
journeys: Access a model → orchestrate work → execute in isolation → persist state → verify results. Permissions and budgets constrain execution.
Develop and debug → evaluate → review access → publish a version. Turn an implementation into a discoverable, traceable asset.
Discover capabilities → verify identity and access → delegate tasks → exchange state and results across explicit boundaries.

taskLoop.title: From intent to outcome
taskLoop.note: Concept demo · select a step to explore
steps: Identify intent, constraints and acceptance criteria with the relevant models and knowledge.
Break down work, arrange dependencies and identify tools, budgets and human checkpoints.
Use tools and sandboxes within granted access, preserving execution state and outputs.
Check outcomes against acceptance criteria. Feed unmet requirements into the next iteration.
